# Wiring routing paths through interior

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Run wires along the driver's side door jamb channel or behind the back seat. [t938]

[Partial] Remove weatherstripping from the top front door opening, then find an A-pillar gap for wire routing. [t236]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Run wires along the driver's side door jamb channel to hide them under carpet or behind plastic panels.

_Procedure reported by [t938]._

## Parts

- Straightened coat hanger: To help maneuver wires through tight spaces [t236]

## Tips & gotchas

- If accessing the rear, run cables behind the back seat and into a channel next to the cargo tray. [t938]
- Peel back weather stripping at that location to access the outside. [t938]
- Find a gap between the body and interior plastic A-pillar piece to feed wires. [t236]
